category_title: Struggling readers of color who voluntarily contribute interpretations during whole-group text discussions
minimal_context: The student is participating in a whole-group discussion about figurative language in the book Teammates.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are reading Teammates. 'Pee Wee's legs felt heavy, but he knew what he had to do.' This is figurative language. Are his legs really heavy?

STUDENT: (Speaking over several seconds of crosstalk) He don't want to do it, and at the same time, he does.

TUTOR: Oh, guys, listen to this. What did you just say?

STUDENT: I don't remember what I just said.

TUTOR: Remember you just said something about him wanting to do it?

STUDENT: (Seeming unsure as peers continue talking over him in the crosstalk) Oh, yeah... he don't want to do it...

options.A: Ask the student an explain story element question about the book during the whole-group discussion.
options.B: Ask the student a follow-up question that links the physical sensation in the text to a potential emotional state.
options.C: Circle back to the student after the interceding talk, evaluate their interpretation as 'good', and invite them to continue interpreting the text.
options.D: Agree with the student that they are having a rough time participating in the whole-group discussion.
